recipes.name: Squash Casserole
ingredients_raw: 0.25 cup water, or more as needed

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x13-inch casserole dish; set aside.
Place squash, onion, and water in a large skillet over medium heat. Cover and cook until squash is tender, about 5 minutes. Drain well and transfer to a large bowl.
Mix cracker crumbs and cheese together in a separate bowl. Stir half of the cracker mixture into cooked squash mixture.
Mix eggs and milk together in a small bowl, then add to squash mixture; stir in 1/4 cup melted butter, and season with salt and pepper. Spread mixture into the prepared baking dish.
Sprinkle with remaining cracker mixture, and dot with 2 tablespoons butter.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown on top and set, about 25 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Squash Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This easy squash casserole combines tender squash with a creamy sauce, topped with a crunchy cracker and cheese topping for a classic Southern side.

video.description: Fresh, tender squash combines with Cheddar cheese, sweet onion, and buttery round crackers for an unforgettably delicious bite. Create this silky crowd-pleaser at home with our top-rated recipe and a few tips from Nicole.

review.reviewBody: Hey yall, this southern girl added bacon sauteed with the onion prior to cooking. I have found squash is always good with bacon, and my husband loves this.

I'd give this 10 stars if I could. My boyfriend's aunt made something similar for us last year and I've been trying to find a recipe like it ever since. This has to be as close as it gets! I followed the recipe except I had to use 2 zucchini (I was out of yellow squash), but the green with the yellow actually looked nice - gave it some color. I HIGHLY recommend this recipe to ANYONE! My mom always made the kind with sour cream and cream of mushroom/chicken soup - this is 10 times better! Thanks!

The first time I made this recipe, I found it to be a little to bland for my taste. To compensate, the next time I made it, I sprinkled the squash liberally with dried oregano while it was steaming, and added a couple of pinches of nutmeg to the squash when adding the cheese and cracker mix. A definite improvement.

Recipe is great. Cooking squash in advance will avoid having a mushy end product, as squash is up to 90% water. Most of the water will evaporate when cooked in the skillet. The small amount of water added in the skillet at the start of cooking it is to prevent scorching/sticking until the squash breaks down and releases its own water. Do not put a lid on the skillet to allow for evaporation. Do not omit the other ingredients unless you substitute. The egg, milk, and cracker crumbs act as binders and thickeners (the flour from the crackers). I do not add the extra salt. Dotting the top with butter is an error- the butter will not melt all over. Dotting of butter such as inside an apple pie will work fine as the top crust will seal the pie and allow the butter to spread but not in this case. The butter will only melt downward from where it is placed. Mix the melted butter with the cracker crumbs then spread on the top. This is a standard type recipe and any type of cooked vegetable or type of cracker can be used if you prefer. If you want it to be outstanding (and extra calories but delicious), use only real butter and heavy cream.

This was absolutely delicious. I used all the ingrediennts with no substitutions but I did use a different method. I layered the raw sliced squash overlaping in the bottom of the baking dish. Sprinkled with salt and pepper, carmelized onions, crushed crackers and cheese. I did this twice and then I topped with a last layer of squash, S&P, egg and milk mixture, and finally the crackerrs and cheese. Covered and baked at 350 for an hour. (actually I cooked it for 40 minutes at 350 and then 20 minutes at 375 b/c it seemed like it wasn't cooking fast enough). The squash was crisp tender and just fantastic! My dh doesn't like squash so it's all for me YAY :)

Yum! I turned it into a full meal by browning some Italian sausage and adding that. I substituted Pepperridge Farms pre-seasoned dressing for the crackers, so I left out the seasonings. I browned it 10 minutes longer than what the recipe called for. It turned out great!

We made this casserole per the recipe. It was delicious. I would give it 5 Stars except a “9x13” dish specified. We used an 8x8x2.25” (2Qt) Pyrex dish with AMPLE room to spare. We weigh ingredients. We consulted a volume to weight converter and got 452 grams (~1Lb) for the 4 Cups of sliced squash. 4 Cups (452g) Sliced Yellow Squash** ½ Cup (80g) Chopped Onion** ¼ Cup Water, Or More As Needed** 35 Ritz Round Crackers, Crushed** 1 Cup (116g) Shredded Cheddar Cheese** 2 Large Eggs, Beaten** ¾ Cup Milk** ¼ Cup (57g) Butter, Melted** 1 tsp Salt** Ground Black Pepper To Taste** 2 Tbls (28g) Butter

Delicious! I did make a couple of changes. Sautéed the squash and onions in a bit of oil with a tsp of salt instead of cooking with water to pull more liquid out of the veggies. Did not find it necessary to add so much melted butter to the squash mixture so only added half and mixed the rest into the cheese and cracker mixture for the topping. Tasty and comforting!

Family love this dish. Perfect for gathering. I already made it twice. I did made some modifications: I add 3 minced garlic and 1 TSP garlic powder to cook along summer squashes and chopped onions. I sautéed with 1TSP oil instead of 1/4 cup water. I also use all ritz cracker/ sharp cheddar mix to mix with squash onion instead of just half of them as recipe indicated because it looks too much liquid . I use another sleeve of ritz crackers mixed with 1/2 cup of sharp cheddar cheese plus 2 TSP melted butter as toppings. But the results is wonderful. A great way for everybody to eat more vegetables!

I used a mix of zucchini and yellow squash sautéed in olive oil with vidalia onion and a couple cloves of garlic. Followed the rest of the recipe but added extra cheese. I didn’t find it overly eggy at all, maybe because of sautéing instead of boiling.

My first ever squash casserole. I’m not a huge yellow squash fan, so I used 1 large yellow and 1 large zucchini. I did add some pablano pepper to the onions and skipped the melted butter, opting to just add some slices of butter on top before cooking. It was EXCELLENT
Excellent! I used one half cup white cheddar and 1/2 cup Gruyere.
This one is a keeper. I had doubts about the liquid measurements in this recipe but it turned out perfectly. I have made plenty of squash casseroles over the years and this one ranks up near the top.
I absolutely love this recipe! There was nothing hard about it at all.
Made it like the recipe.It is so good it does not need any changes.
Excellent recipe that works well with zucchini or yellow squash!
I used multiple squashes from our garden and we loved it.
Only thing I changed was I added 4 slices of cooked crumbled bacon. It was perfect! Very easy to make.
I added a can of Cream of mushroom soup.
I didn't have yellow squash so I used butternut squash. This dish is very easy to make. I did also add some garlic powder, paprika and cinnamon. This is delicious and a keeper. Loved it!
